<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915996_theRebbe_995" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915996_theRebbe_995__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the second division, that of "smallness," as it applies to the categories of "your little ones," "your wives," and "your stranger," representing progressively lower levels of Divine service.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And afterwards, in the second verse, he explains the second division,</t>
    <t s="1">which is in the aspect of smallness (katnut).</t>
    <t s="2">And he begins with the matter of "your little ones" (tafkhem),</t>
    <t s="3">which is in the aspect of the smallness of the intellect that is extremely constricted in the smallness of the emotions, which are the aspect of "the lesser countenances" (Anpin Zutra),</t>
    <t s="4">like the infant in a person, who is not of complete intellect.</t>
    <t s="5">And "your wives" (n'sheikhem) is the aspect of the smallness of the aspect of the receiver, etc.</t>
    <t s="6">And afterwards it says, "and your stranger who is in the midst of your camp, from your woodchopper to your water-drawer,"</t>
    <t s="7">for these three levels are the aspect of the most external levels, which are the animal and natural soul, etc.,</t>
    <t s="8">analogous to the stranger (ger) who is drawn from the nations of the world, etc.</t>
    <t s="9">(In addition to the fact that the matter of the stranger, simply understood, is in the aspect of smallness,</t>
    <t s="10">and as our sages, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="11">"A convert who converts is like a newborn child"),</t>
    <t s="12">which, from its own side, is distant from G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="13">and nevertheless it is brought close under the wings of the Shechinah, like a convert who actually converts.</t>
    <t s="14">And concerning this it says, "and your stranger who is in the midst of your camp,"</t>
    <t s="15">that it is separate from the innerness of G-dliness that is in the souls of Israel, which are called "the man of Israel above,"</t>
    <t s="16">but rather it is caught and dragged in the midst of your camp as a subsidiary to the main thing.</t>
    <t s="17">And this is what it means that he performs physical labor, like chopping wood and drawing water,</t>
    <t s="18">for chopping wood is only like a preparation for cooking,</t>
    <t s="19">and likewise drawing water is only like a subsidiary and aid to eating,</t>
    <t s="20">as is understood from what is explained elsewhere,</t>
    <t s="21">that the entire matter of drinking is only so that the blood created through eating will spread throughout the limbs</t>
    <t s="22">(and this is the explanation of our sages' statement,</t>
    <t s="23">"If one ate and did not drink, his eating is blood"),</t>
    <t s="24">and so it is regarding spiritual eating, which is the mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="25">And thus,</t>
    <t s="26">these three last levels enumerated here are according to how the G-dly soul descended and became clothed below, below, in the animal soul,</t>
    <t s="27">"You descended to Egypt," etc.</t>
    <t s="28">And even regarding these levels it is written, "You are standing today, all of you, before Hashem, your G-d."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section questions how the "stranger" can stand before Hashem, and explains that "standing" (nitzavim) implies elevation and governance, enabling even the lowest levels to be elevated through the ascent of the souls of Israel.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And he continues there,</t>
    <t s="2">"But behold, at first glance this is a great wonder,</t>
    <t s="3">for it is understandable that the souls can stand before Hashem,</t>
    <t s="4">but 'your stranger who is in the midst of your camp'—</t>
    <t s="5">how can they also stand before Hashem?"</t>
    <t s="6">And he explains regarding this,</t>
    <t s="7">that this is the matter of "you are standing" (atem nitzavim) specifically,</t>
    <t s="8">for the meaning of "nitzavim" is a matter of rising and elevation,</t>
    <t s="9">like "my sheaf arose and also stood upright,"</t>
    <t s="10">and like a standing stone (matzevah) that is placed on the ground, which one erects and sets up as a monument,</t>
    <t s="11">like the monument of Yaakov, about which it is written,</t>
    <t s="12">"And he took the stone... and placed it as a monument."</t>
    <t s="13">And so is the matter here,</t>
    <t s="14">that what is written "you are standing today" refers to Rosh Hashanah,</t>
    <t s="15">for then "all of you are standing today,"</t>
    <t s="16">and as it is written,</t>
    <t s="17">"And He was King in Yeshurun, when the heads of the people gathered, the tribes of Israel together,"</t>
    <t s="18">for on Rosh Hashanah, the souls of Israel ascend to their root, where they are all "all of you" as one, like a single entity</t>
    <t s="19">(as explained in Likkutei Torah, Parshat Nitzavim),</t>
    <t s="20">and as explained in Tanya, chapter 32, that when they are in their root, they are all compatible, and "one Father of all of them," and who knows their greatness and level in their root and source, etc.</t>
    <t s="21">And he continues there,</t>
    <t s="22">"And furthermore, the matter of 'nitzavim' will be interpreted as a term of dominion and rulership,</t>
    <t s="23">like 'and he placed governors (netzivim) in Edom,'</t>
    <t s="24">and like 'the governor (netziv) of the Philistines,'</t>
    <t s="25">which is a minister who rules over the province,</t>
    <t s="26">and likewise the one appointed over the workers in a craft is called a 'netziv,'</t>
    <t s="27">like 'the youth who was set over the reapers.'</t>
    <t s="28">And through this it will be understood how it is possible that even 'your stranger and your woodchopper, etc.' will be 'standing' (nitzavim) before Hashem literally,</t>
    <t s="29">for since the souls of Israel ascend to their first source, etc.,</t>
    <t s="30">from there it can illuminate even the portion of the G-dly soul that is clothed in a coarse garment, etc.,</t>
    <t s="31">so that they too will rise and stand before Hashem literally.</t>
    <t s="32">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="33">that this is the reason the discourse brings these verses</t>
    <t s="34">[and not the verse 'netziv' said regarding Shlomo,</t>
    <t s="35">and also not the verse 'the king's deputy' (netziv melech),</t>
    <t s="36">as is usual in many places],</t>
    <t s="37">in order to hint that the elevation of "nitzavim" exists also in "your stranger"</t>
    <t s="38">(the animal soul drawn from the aspect of the nations of the world),</t>
    <t s="39">like "and he placed governors in Edom" and "the governor of the Philistines,"</t>
    <t s="40">that even the "governors" are from Edom and the Philistines,</t>
    <t s="41">and nevertheless they are "governors" (nitzavim)</t>
    <t s="42">[and he did not bring the verse "and there was no king in Edom, a deputy king,"</t>
    <t s="43">for its meaning is that the deputy is in place of a king,</t>
    <t s="44">and this is negated in the discourse regarding the stranger].</t>
    <t s="45">And also regarding "your woodchopper and your water-drawer,"</t>
    <t s="46">like "the youth who was set over the reapers,"</t>
    <t s="47">that even though he too is among the workers in the craft,</t>
    <t s="48">nevertheless</t>
    <t s="49">(since he is appointed over them)</t>
    <t s="50">he is a "netziv" (standing/appointed).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the difference between the unity achieved from below on Rosh Hashanah and the unity drawn from above on Yom Kippur, paralleling the two types of unity at the giving of the Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And he continues there,</t>
    <t s="2">"It still needs to be understood what is meant by the expression 'all of you' (kulchem),</t>
    <t s="3">which implies that all of Israel are standing in a state of inclusion, all as one man,</t>
    <t s="4">unlike the verse 'And He was King in Yeshurun, when the heads of the people gathered,' which implies that the main inclusion is specifically in the 'heads of the people,'</t>
    <t s="5">for the gathering is through the heads.</t>
    <t s="6">And also, what is the meaning of the expression 'when they gather' (b'hit'asef),</t>
    <t s="7">which implies that they will gather of their own accord,</t>
    <t s="8">and not that one needs to gather them and connect them together.</t>
    <t s="9">And he explains regarding this,</t>
    <t s="10">that what is written 'you are standing, all of you,'</t>
    <t s="11">even though it refers to Rosh Hashanah, when all the souls of Israel become included together, etc.,</t>
    <t s="12">behold, this is the matter of inclusion as it is from the side of the recipients,</t>
    <t s="13">who ascend from below to above,</t>
    <t s="14">and concerning this it is written,</t>
    <t s="15">'His left hand is under my head'</t>
    <t s="16">(of the Congregation of Israel),</t>
    <t s="17">to lift them up and elevate them above.</t>
    <t s="18">But there is an aspect of unity that is effected from the side of the revelation from above,</t>
    <t s="19">in the manner of 'His right hand embraces me,'</t>
    <t s="20">and this is on Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="21">and as it is written,</t>
    <t s="22">'On the third day He will raise us up, and we will live before Him,'</t>
    <t s="23">for this unification is from the side of the revelation of the influencer,</t>
    <t s="24">which acts first upon the 'heads of the people,'</t>
    <t s="25">and even regarding this it is written 'when they gather' (b'hit'asef), in a manner of spontaneity,</t>
    <t s="26">for it is done spontaneously from the side of the revelation of the influencer.</t>
    <t s="27">And these two matters also existed at the time of the giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="28">for initially it is written,</t>
    <t s="29">'And Israel encamped there,'</t>
    <t s="30">as one man with one heart,</t>
    <t s="31">which is the matter of unity from the side of the recipient,</t>
    <t s="32">which was on Rosh Chodesh Sivan,</t>
    <t s="33">and afterwards there was the matter of unity that was effected on the very day of the giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="34">when it is written,</t>
    <t s="35">'And Hashem descended upon Mount Sinai,'</t>
    <t s="36">which was a revelation of the Awtsmoos,</t>
    <t s="37">and from this was effected the matter of unity in its ultimate,</t>
    <t s="38">'when the heads of the people gathered.'</t>
    <t s="39">And so it is on Yom Kippur, which is also a time of the giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="40">the day on which the latter tablets were given.</t>
    <t s="41">And this is the true matter of 'you are standing today, all of you, before Hashem,'</t>
    <t s="42">meaning before Hashem literally,</t>
    <t s="43">concerning which it is written,</t>
    <t s="44">'On the third day He will raise us up, and we will live before Him.'</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
